clue.text: Meet in a bar

definitions.meaning: to meet an argument or attack is to answer or oppose it
a shop or pub bar across which goods and drinks are served

explanation.surface: An invitation to rendezvous at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a charge is to oppose it with a response; a shop's serving bar has the same name.

clue.text: Rotter in US intelligence is a chirpy type

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, the rotter going into the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
a rotter is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A bad egg working for American spies turns out to be cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotter' and 'chirpy' pull towards a cheery villain; the agency is cut open after its second letter, with the clue's 'a' supplying the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is an insect famous for the shrill chirping song the males make.

clue.text: Forget a French king's name

parts.note: un is French for a
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Someone fails to recall what a French monarch was called.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlearn something is to deliberately drop knowledge, a synonym of forgetting it.

clue.text: Norse god is held by woman to rule with an iron hand

definitions.text: to rule with an iron hand

parts.note: Tyr is the Norse god of war

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the woman's name, as though she were holding it

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian deity, gripped by a lady, governs harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a despot, wielding power cruelly, is a tyrant's way of ruling with an iron hand.

clue.text: Religious revolution helping to usher in English ceremony

indicators.note: to usher someone in is to lead them inside, so the helping surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a helping or portion of food is a ration
a form is a set ritual or ceremony, as in a form of service

explanation.surface: A church upheaval assists in bringing in an English rite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reformation was the sixteenth-century upheaval that split Western Christianity into Catholic and Protestant churches.

clue.text: Weapon replacing the mace

indicators.note: the letters of the words are placed anew, put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: One arm substitutes for an old club-like weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' signals the rearrangement of THE MACE, which also fits the surface of one weapon succeeding another.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used as a tool and sometimes as a weapon.

clue.text: This could keep you dry as river's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A rainproof garment is handy when the river floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns CAM upward in this down entry; MAC is short for mackintosh, a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a waterproof raincoat, which protects its wearer from rain.

clue.text: Get hold of spiteful woman before church

indicators.note: the woman comes first, ahead of the church

parts.note: a cat is slang for a malicious woman

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a nasty lady before she reaches church.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something is to grasp or seize it.

clue.text: Outside theatre, capital raised for so called musical work

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the combined letters read upward
the capital is placed around the theatre

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
rep, short for repertory, is a theatre company or theatre

explanation.surface: Something about a city's stage being elevated, connected with a famous piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' and 'raised' work on the combined letters, which read upward in this down entry. Beethoven's fifth piano concerto is nicknamed the Emperor, hence 'so called'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Concerto No. 5 is popularly known by this name, so the musical work is so called.

clue.text: Drink served in Conservatives' Press Office

indicators.note: the drink is offered within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Coffee is handed round at a party's media department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' signals letters lying within the words: conservativES PRESS Office.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: State opening mostly generating heat

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: an orifice is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A ceremonial launch that is warming in effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of ORIFICE. CAL is a standard abbreviation for the US state of California.
explanation.definitionFit: Calorific means producing heat or energy, as in the calorific value of a fuel.

clue.text: Give more drink to young boxer, say

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Someone refills a glass for a juvenile fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests the ring, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass is to refill it, giving its owner more to drink.

clue.text: Portrayed doctor with beard

parts.note: an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A painting depicts a bearded medic.
explanation.walkthrough: AWN is the botanical name for the beard of a cereal grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn has been depicted in a sketch or picture.

clue.text: Perhaps Arab people developed shore?

parts.note: a people or nation is a race

indicators.note: the letters of the word are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A question about whether an Arab population built up its coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person, but here it is a breed of horse; 'developed' rearranges SHORE as HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a breed of fast horse, so it is an example of an animal bred for racing.

clue.text: Result of oversewing?

parts.note: read oversewing as over-sowing of clergy: planting too many priests leads to the church having too much influence

explanation.surface: What happens when a seam is stitched over.
explanation.walkthrough: The needlework picture misleads; the pun is on sowing too many clerics, producing a system dominated by the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: This term describes a policy that gives the clergy excessive power, the imagined outcome of overplanting priests.

clue.text: Disorder creating pain so!

indicators.note: putting letters into disorder means jumbling them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An ailment that causes this much discomfort!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' rearranges CREATING PAIN SO, and the whole clue also describes the heart condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina pectoris is a heart condition causing chest pain when the heart muscle lacks oxygen.

clue.text: Four identical notes about a confidential meeting

indicators.note: the repeated notes go around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, here written four times

explanation.surface: Four matching musical tones surround a private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the note of the sol-fa scale also spelt TI; four of them go around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, French for head to head, is a private conversation between two people.

clue.text: Work painter said he could help one see better

definitions.text: he could help one see better

parts.note: op, from opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: the painter's name is spoken, giving the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: An artist's creation is claimed to improve someone's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives the sound of TITIAN, pronounced tish-un, spelt here TICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and supplies glasses or lenses to correct vision.

clue.text: Cabinet-makers one's employed in the best church buildings

parts.note: prime means the best, as in prime cuts

indicators.note: the one is put to work inside the church buildings

parts.note: minsters are large churches, often former monastery churches
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Carpenters have a job in the finest cathedrals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet-makers' suggests joiners, but it means those who appoint a government cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of government choose the ministers who sit in the cabinet, so they literally form cabinets.

clue.text: Spread complaint about Liberal decline?

indicators.note: the spreading of disease goes round the party's letter

parts.note: to infect is to pass on a disease

explanation.surface: A political fall described as a contagious disease affecting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' suggests a slump, but in grammar to decline a noun is to give its forms, which is what inflecting does.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, to inflect a noun is to change its endings for case, which is also called declining it.

clue.text: Intend to split regular payments for dress

indicators.note: the aim breaks the payments apart by sitting in the middle

parts.note: rent is paid regularly for a home
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone plans to divide their periodic bills to buy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old, literary word for clothing or attire.

clue.text: Raise provided as business calamity ensues

indicators.note: in a down clue raising the word means reading it upward

parts.note: if means provided, on condition that
Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A firm suffers disaster after an attempt to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns IF upward in this down entry to give FI; AS is the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete disaster.

clue.text: Fashionable passage to New Zealand attracts a complaint

parts.note: in means fashionable
a flue is a passage for smoke

explanation.surface: A trendy route to the Antipodes draws a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza is an illness, and a complaint is a general word for ailment.

clue.text: Extremist last month given right to have article

parts.note: ult, ultimo, means of last month in old business letters
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fanatic was granted the right to own a piece of writing recently.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old commercial shorthand for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a hardliner.

clue.text: Decisive defence one needed after jumping bail

indicators.note: the one is put last, following the jumbled letters
the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A suspect who skipped bail needs a cast-iron story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping bail' reads as absconding but signals rearranging BAIL to ALIB.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof that one was elsewhere when a crime happened, a conclusive defence.

clue.text: Useless record held by silly nit

indicators.note: the record is gripped between the letters of the jumbled word
silly means the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A worthless disc is clutched by a foolish idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles the insult into INT before the record goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means incompetent or ineffective, without skill.

clue.text: Very valuable diamonds left in cupboard

indicators.note: the jewels and the side go inside the cupboard

parts.note: a press is a cupboard, especially for linen
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Precious gems have been left in a cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless means so precious that no price could be put on it.

clue.text: Parking? That's an easy thing

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A remark that finding a parking space is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Something as easy as pie is very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom easy as pie, the dish stands for something simple.

clue.text: Compound charge in hours of darkness, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: a night rate is a fee charged at night

explanation.surface: Costs for overnight work are discussed by listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical salt containing the NO3 group, so it is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Conductor needs a little time to take a rest when agitated

indicators.note: shaken up, the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader needs a break when stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when agitated' rearranges MO plus A REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor.
